name: sleep_wake
note: The daemon is STOPPED mid-scenario, because that is the only way this board ever sleeps. Quiet data is not a quiet host: dispatch() stamps last_host_ms on any host protocol line (proto.c:262) and the daemon answers every 10s ping with a pong (bridge.py:145-149), so a live daemon cannot leave the board 30s silent (HOST_TIMEOUT_MS, proto.c:29) at any poll interval -- an earlier version of this file asked for a 40s gap between steps and would have passed against firmware with sleep deleted. With the daemon gone for 45s the board loses the host, sleeps, and must wake and apply a fresh frame when the daemon returns. The evidence is tap_asserts.WOKE_MARKER, printed nowhere but where ui_sleep_run()'s sleep loop exits; the earlier lines of the cycle are printed while nothing holds the port and are lost. CONFIRMED on the Windows desk 2026-09-07: the board slept and woke at 77.0s and applied a fresh frame at 78.0s -- the run failed only because the marker written down here was a sentence the firmware has never printed. The steps replay from the start in the second daemon -- ScriptedProvider stamps its t0 at construction -- which is why min_tx is twice the step count.
